q: I wonder if the older parents who tell me "you're going to miss these days" remember the crying, screaming, meltdowns, how exhausted they were, how needed they were every second of the day during those days or if they remember just the good parts of it lol.
cx: Work-from-home father of a 6- and 3-year-old, both home all summer.

q: I am not going to spend thousands to parent somewhere else and have to take all the baby shit with me on the way.
cx: Refuses to fly with the children until the meltdowns ease.

q: I’m actually scared of her, every week I’ve got new scratches on my face and arms.
cx: Solo working mother of a 2-year-old with intense meltdowns and broken sleep.

q: I try to talk her down or cuddle her and it’s pointless, if I growl that also does nothing. The only way it stops it literally to just ignore her but even that’s losing effectiveness.
cx: Same mother on what she tries in a meltdown.

q: Respectfully, please don’t give advice if you haven’t experienced an intense toddler or say this is normal, it’s not normal or at the least it’s the intense end of normal.
cx: Rejects 'it's normal' reassurance in advance.

q: I get no break, I’m a solo working parent.
cx: Same mother; the child stays up while she finishes work.

q: I’m constantly being told she might be on the spectrum but I’ve tried to get medical advice and they all say she’s completely fine and is too young for evaluation anyway.
cx: What people around her keep suggesting.

q: She’s completely fine at daycare, they haven’t reported any behavioural issues with me.
cx: The intensity appears only with her.

q: Has anyone tried setting a timer once things got tougher with wearing clothing? I know its not in oh crap method but I am curious if doing so will help my son experience some success with pants...
cx: Day 3 of Oh Crap with a 2.5-year-old; block 2 brought accidents.

q: I hate how at the end of some days I feel like a pos mom for getting overwhelmed & overstimulated.. mom guilt sucks.
cx: First-time mother of a very high-energy 18-month-old.

q: So many of our friends with kids his age, have such chill kids— then there’s my feral toddler. 🫠
cx: Same mother.

q: She was kind of judgy and told me, "Your daughter is super smart and very old. She knows the difference and you're being too nice every time she poops in her underwear."
cx: A friend's verdict on her gentle response to poop accidents, under a week into training.

q: I'm going to continue being nice. I don't want to shame my toddler for pooping in her undies. Here's what I say when she poops in them: I say, "It's okay, it's just a mistake. It's a little oopsie."
cx: Same mother defends her script.

q: I tried talking to her nicely, rewarding her, bribing her — nothing works.
cx: Pee trained; poop in underwear days 4–6.

q: We’ve done bubbles, blow out the candle, water running, feet in water but she just can’t release.
cx: Two weeks into Oh Crap with a 33-month-old who holds pee all day.

q: Should we stop and try again in a few months?
cx: Same parent.

q: If anything she ended up getting to the point where she pees herself and doesn’t even care anymore! […] I’ve put her in a pull up so basically we’re in diapers again.
cx: Five days later, after following advice to ignore the holding.

q: So, we have tried everything. The three day oh crap method, timers, stickers, toys, undies, reminders, no reminders. He refuses to poop in the toilet and always has.
cx: Three months training a boy who started at 2 years 4 months.

q: Daycare and us are out of ideas.  We started potty training because he was interested (at about 2 years 4 months). Its been three months of hell.  We are now officially taking a break
cx: Same parent pausing with the daycare's agreement.

q: Not the basics (stickers, reminders). I want the crazy stuff, the weird stuff, the random stuff.
cx: Asks strangers for what the standard advice lacks.

q: whenever I tell my mom that things are difficult, she just says “oh you were a difficult child too” or whenever I speak to other moms I don’t feel like they share the same problems
cx: Mother of a high-need 14-month-old in rural Switzerland; family an hour away.

q: He will go to daycare full-time. It’s so hard for me to imagine that he will be going to daycare so much, but at the same time I feel some sort of relief but also I feel like a bad mom
cx: Returning to work in September after a layoff.

q: They really live their life, their best life while I’m just trying to survive and today just cancel plans again because he’s in such a bad mood
cx: Same mother on other mothers.

q: I also feel guilty because my husband and I try to be present for our 3 year old but some days I don’t feel like I have anything left after stressing about the baby all day.
cx: 3-year-old pushing, hitting and biting since a sister arrived 3.5 months ago.

q: I just feel like I’ve totally botched the transition from 1-2 and don’t know how to climb out of this hole and way of thinking.
cx: Same mother.

q: We are fortunate to not spend money on childcare. If I had to put my kids in daycare, it wouldn't make sense for me to work anymore.
cx: Parent of a 3-year-old and a 9-month-old; grandparents cover three workdays.

q: I almost canceled disappointment because I knew that it would be me paying my $40 copay to answer a questionnaire that I could have found online.
cx: A well-child check where the doctor questioned the child's socialising.

q: She started making me feel like a bad parent. My kid is ridiculously smart and excels in almost all other areas but she didn't seem to care about the positives
cx: On the doctor's manner at the check-up.

q: In the last week and a half we’ve noticed some behavioral challenges popping up (more tantrums, difficulty going to bed, waking up crying at night, etc).
cx: Two weeks into Oh Crap with a 2.5-year-old.

q: its extremely embarrassing to be in social groups with such an angry kid, i dont want people to think im an angry person towards him or “you know where he gets it from” kind of situation
cx: Mother of a 4-year-old and a 17-month-old who hits and grabs at playgroup.

q: his nanny has even commented on his behavior being “intense” especially during social-play like situations.
cx: Same mother; the nanny noticed too.

q: alot of kids at the park or his group dont play with him since he was about.. 14mo old because hes so mean, and i feel so singled out as a mother
cx: Same mother.

q: i took parenting classes for about 2.5 years because i was young when i had my daughter. i know alot about early childhood development. ive always been told connection is the best way to get a child to listen.
cx: Trained in parenting classes; approach works for her daughter, not her son.

q: asking him to breathe or practice grounding techniques just does not work. […] its just not a skill that he understands even when its demonstrated.
cx: Calming techniques taught from 8 months failed on this child.

q: every kid is different and not very many kids will just sit down and breathe
cx: Same mother on why one technique doesn't fit both children.

q: My husband and I are very anxious about this whole thing and are dreading my son crying for days on end because we took the binky away.
cx: Planning a 'binky fairy' weekend for a 2.5-year-old while the father is off work.

q: The night consisted of constant tantrums. Food arrive an hour after ordering. Him not liking his food. No play area. It was awful. I could feel the tears coming in my eyes. In the end we left before everyone else.
cx: Alone with a 16-month-old at a friend's birthday dinner.
